what: the task states an accepted form AND a rejection rule; the visible suite checks only well-formed inputs, and the habitual regex implementation silently accepts malformed ones
expectedOutcome: the visible suite is GREEN on the base, on the known-good and on the known-bad. The known-bad is the HABITUAL implementation — find the hours group, find the minutes group, add them — which is what a competent engineer writes when the visible tests show only well-formed inputs. It violates the stated rule that anything not well-formed must throw: "1h30" returns 60 instead of throwing, "90" returns 0, "1x" returns 60, "m90" returns 90. Only the hidden oracle exercises the rejection rule.
measuredScope: This is the sharpest version of the partial-implementation class in this corpus: the wrong answer is not a strawman but the LIKELY answer, reached by habit (parseInt/loose regex) rather than by carelessness. The previous pilot showed a plain agent solving every purpose-built trap; this fixture targets the one thing those traps did not require — reading the REJECTION half of a specification and treating it as part of the requirement.
requirements: parseDuration accepts a sequence of <number><unit> groups with h or m units and returns minutes
anything not of that form must throw an error containing "invalid duration"
a trailing bare number ("1h30") is refused, not partially parsed
a unit without a number ("m90") is refused
leading zeros ("01h") and repeated groups ("1h1h") are allowed
benchmarkConfigNote: Category B (partial implementation, sharpened so the wrong answer is the likely one). This field names the configuration to USE: guarded WITHOUT --register-requirements, because that measures the correctness axis cleanly. PROVENANCE OF THE EXISTING PILOT: it ran this fixture WITH --register-requirements (7 requirements registered), which the guard now REJECTS - nothing binds those requirements to a sealed check, so the Stop hook refuses correct work and those trials carry the harness's requirementConfiguration caveat. Their guarded NOT PROVEN verdicts must not be read as Amabie judging the code; their token and oracle figures are sound. No trial exists yet under the clean configuration, so the fixture's correctness measurement is still to be taken. See docs/V1.2-PLAN.md open items 6 and 7.
